page: Amazon Web Services t3.micro is an entry-level burstable instance deployed on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance configuration exposes 2 virtual CPUs mapped to a single physical core via hyperthreading. Cache architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AVX-512, and AES instructions. Compute resources are provided under a burstable CPU credit allocation model.

System memory comprises 1.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, providing 0.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage for persistent disk needs. Baseline network bandwidth is listed at 0 Gbps, with networking capabilities scaling burstably according to Nitro hypervisor network resource balancing.

Across benchmark evaluations, the t3.micro registers in the lowest percentiles for sustained throughput. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests yield scores of 1018.99 and 1350.29 respectively, constrained by the burstable CPU envelope. Memory bandwidth achieves 6.9 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 11.3 GB/sec for writes. Workload-specific benchmarks reflect these operational boundaries, recording 1.39 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.76 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Because of its shared-core model and low base capacity, the t3.micro offers high cost efficiency for lightweight tasks that run intermittently rather than continuously. It serves as an economical platform for low-traffic web applications, small microservices, lightweight development sandboxes, and administrative bastion hosts that do not demand sustained compute performance or high memory density.
